# Progress summary

The experimental design is as follows: image-only ScienceQA (`lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG`) for main experiments and text-only as secondary analysis; the softmax-over-options variant as an additional ablation alongside $k=8$ sampling; oracle and $\tau=0$ baselines for the consistency-filter comparison; VQAv2 as a stretch goal only. All six action items were completed.

| Action item | Owner | Status |
|---|-|----|
| Confirm SCF GPU allocation | Matt | Done --- TITAN Xp (12 GB), CUDA 12.8, `PreemptMode=REQUEUE` |
| Set up Python env; confirm SmolVLM loads | Matt | Done --- conda `smolvlm` (Python 3.11), torch 2.14.1+cu126; 507.48M params at bf16 |
| HF Hub repo for checkpoints | Matt | Done --- `mattbix/cs289-smolvlm-checkpoints` |
| Zero-shot greedy baseline, 500-question subset | Matt | Done --- 0.6480 (324/500) |
| ScienceQA counts, image+text vs. text-only, per split | Matt, Shiqi | Done --- Matt ran, Shiqi independently reproduced |
| Softmax-over-options API notes | Matt, Shiqi | Done --- `02_softmax_eval.py`; Shiqi's check found the read-position issue |

Two infrastructure notes. The proposal assumed an A100 or L4 (24 GB); the available GPU was a single TITAN Xp (12 GB), and SmolVLM-500M's ~1.1 GB bf16 footprint meant LoRA fit comfortably, so the proposal's assumption did not need to be met. The `PreemptMode=REQUEUE` partition required per-example checkpointing, which both baseline scripts did (JSONL append after every question); and the HF Hub token, stored under `$HOME`, survived login-node changes, with `HF_HOME` exported from `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` to cover both `srun` and `sbatch`.

# Preliminary results

## Dataset counts

| Dataset | Split | Total | Image+text | Text-only |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` | train | 6,218 | 6,218 | 0 |
| | validation | 2,097 | 2,097 | 0 |
| | test | 2,017 | 2,017 | 0 |
| `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` | test | 4,241 | 2,017 | 2,224 |

The `derek-thomas/ScienceQA` image+text column matched `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG` row-for-row on the test split. The main experiments therefore used `lmms-lab/ScienceQA-IMG`; the text-only rows were held out for a secondary analysis.

## Baseline (500-question image-only test subset, seed 0)

| Variant | Accuracy | Forward passes per question |
|---|---:|---|
| Zero-shot greedy | 0.6480 (324/500) | 1 autoregressive decode, $\leq 8$ tokens |

The zero-shot greedy baseline was evaluated on a 500-question random subset of the image-only test split, seed 0 so the subset is reproducible; for the fine-tuning experiments, the validation split would be used for tuning and the test split reserved for final evaluation.

## Softmax variant --- read-position issue, and no significant difference from greedy

The initial softmax script read the answer distribution at the last position of the input prompt, immediately after the literal `"Answer:"` string. Shiqi's independent check found that at that position the model's top token was `" Answer"` on 48 of 50 questions, and the option letters held only a small fraction of the probability. That read position measured a different decision point, not a better-calibrated one, so the 0.6700 figure from the initial 500-question run was withdrawn. Shiqi's corrected version, which prefills `" Answer:"` in the assistant turn and reads the logits after that, agreed with greedy on 48 of 50 questions in his 50-question check. Separately, the initial 59-vs-48 greedy/softmax disagreement count was not statistically significant (McNemar $p \approx 0.3$), so neither finding supports the "softmax captures information greedy misses" reading. The $k=8$ sampling variant has not yet been run; the "complementary signals" question depends on that comparison and is deferred to the post-Nov-6 experiments.

# Remaining work, outline, and code

Beyond the timeline above: the corrected softmax full-500 run (optional), the $k=8$ sampled-mode baseline, the consistency-filter fine-tuning with oracle and $\tau=0$ comparisons, SmolVLM pseudo-label generation on the training split, LoRA fine-tuning with validation-tuning and held-out test evaluation, and the post-fine-tuning re-run of both baselines. The single SCF TITAN Xp was sufficient for SmolVLM-500M inference and LoRA fine-tuning; the course's \$300 in Databricks credits were identified as a backup for longer runs or parallelism if the SCF partition became contended.
